rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 is the best raced design (score 306.5). It finished 10 of 20 oval trials, but every s-bend and slalom trial ended off track (progress 0.39 and 0.28). Mean rms_error is only about 0.02, while max_error reaches the 0.06 m off-track limit. The robot tracks well on average and then fails in sudden bends. Iteration 4 showed that higher kp hurts the harder tracks, so kp stays at 3.0. Line_loss_events near 1 per run mostly reflects the terminal off-track event.

Change: move all five sensors forward from y = 0.03 to y = 0.05 m, keeping the x spacing (-0.04 to 0.04, 16 mm footprints). The hypothesis is turn-in lag: the sensors currently see the tape only after the axle has already reached the bend, so correction arrives late. Reading the line 2 cm earlier should reduce max_error at the sharp alternating bends. Speed (1.3), kp (3.0), kd (0.8), ki (0.02), mass (0.6 kg) and line-loss mode are unchanged, so this iteration tests one variable against the best baseline.

Expected result: max_error on the s-bend and slalom falls below 0.06 more often, and progress on those tracks rises above 0.4 and 0.3 respectively. Oval completion should hold at about 1 in 2.

Hypotheses and next checks: (a) if the s-bend and slalom still exit off track with max_error at 0.06 and sensor y has no effect, the limit is steering authority, so kp should rise slightly to about 3.3 with kd held. (b) If steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 after the move, the forward sensors are amplifying jitter, so kd should drop to about 0.6. (c) If progress stalls below 0.3 with no off-track exit, base_speed is too low for the 3 s limit and should rise toward 1.5.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness, so that the sensor-position effect can be separated from the damping and speed effects.
